definitions.explanation: A formal prayer or ritual performed to ask for divine blessing, healing, protection, or other spiritual favor. Often performed by a priest or religious practitioner at a shrine or temple.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{祈祷|きとう}を{受|う}ける。
examples.english: To receive a prayer at a shrine.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}{祈願|きがん}の{祈祷|きとう}をお{願|ねが}いした。
examples.english: I requested a prayer for safety.

examples.japanese: {新年|しんねん}に{家族|かぞく}で{祈祷|きとう}を{受|う}けに{行|い}くのが{毎年|まいとし}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: It is our annual custom to go as a family to receive a New Year's prayer.

notes:
A formal religious prayer or ritual, typically performed by a Shinto priest ({神主|かんぬし}) at a shrine or by a Buddhist priest at a temple. The person requesting the prayer usually pays a fee ({初穂料|はつほりょう} at Shinto shrines).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祈祷|きとう}を{受|う}ける: to receive a prayer (from a priest)
- {祈祷|きとう}を{行|おこな}う: to perform a prayer
- {祈祷|きとう}{料|りょう}: prayer fee
- {祈祷|きとう}{師|し}: prayer healer; spiritual practitioner
- {安全|あんぜん}{祈祷|きとう}: prayer for safety

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {祈祷|きとう} is commonly performed at life milestones and seasonal events: {初詣|はつもうで} (New Year's shrine visit), {七五三|しちごさん} (children's festival), {車|くるま}の{祈祷|きとう} (blessing of a new car), and {地鎮祭|じちんさい} (ground-breaking ceremony). It is distinct from personal, informal prayer.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {祈|いの}り: prayer — more general and personal; can be done by anyone
- お{参|まい}り: visiting a shrine/temple to pray — the visit itself rather than a formal ritual
- {祈願|きがん}: votive prayer — making a specific wish or request to a deity
